summary: An explicit calculation does not support the record's statement that exchanging the momentum graviton X produces the dark-matter gate. #11 §7 builds X as one massive spin-2 field on spacetime. Every χ–χ–X vertex then sees only the momentum transferred along one χ line, so at fixed transfer the amplitude depends on the incoming relative momentum k only through a polynomial of at most second degree in k². That polynomial's scale is the χ mass. It reaches order one only near 0.8c, changes the amplitude by 2.4×10⁻⁷ at 120 km/s, and no such polynomial normalized to 1 at k = 0 stays below 0.90 in magnitude between 171 and 1500 km/s. The pole part of the exchange is fixed (a d-wave Legendre polynomial) and the non-pole part is a polynomial contact term; a Gaussian or rational function of k sitting on a single-particle pole would need particles of every spin. The crossed (u-channel) term for identical χ is rational in k, but it only halves the forward amplitude and is the same short-range force seen at backward angles; the s-channel term exists only for χχ̄ and vanishes at threshold. In field-theory terms, #6 §4's fiber overlap has two readings. Read as an overlap of the two quanta's phase-space densities, it is exactly an ordinary short-range potential of range ħ/μ ≈ 10 pm, and its cross-section tail is a power law even for Gaussian profiles. Read as an overlap in the relative momentum of the incoming pair, it does give the gate, but it is then a nonlocal four-χ pair interaction with no X pole, mediated if at all by a doubly charged s-channel object rather than by X. The record constructs neither: it has no vertex, fiber profile, dual-stress formula or X propagator on the fibers, and its section condition makes every field independent of the fiber coordinates. The vacuum polarization is Lorentz-invariant in Lorentzian signature, so it cannot supply the missing structure; a preferred frame could, but the resulting gate tracks a pair's velocity through that frame, not the relative velocity. #6 §4's 'rational gates from tree-level exchange' describes rational dependence on the momentum transfer, which is ordinary light-mediator Yukawa physics, not a gate in k. The tag [D — mechanism; shape [O]] is therefore unsupported. The gate and μ should carry [P], with the mechanism [O] and tree-level X-exchange recorded as excluded [D][V]. §14 item 4 asks only about the shape and presupposes an X propagator on momentum fibers that §7 does not have, so it does not cover what is missing.

claims.statement: For on-shell χ, any χ(p_in)–χ(p_out)–X vertex (local, derivative or form-factor) depends Lorentz-invariantly only on t = (p_in − p_out)², since p_in·p_out = m² − t/2. This includes nonlocal smeared bilinears such as a fiber-weighted 'dual stress': the Wigner fiber coordinate of a χ*χ bilinear is the average momentum (p_in + p_out)/2, so a fiber weight w becomes w(m² − t/4).

Since s − u = 4m² + 8k² − q², at fixed transfer q the dependence on the incoming relative momentum k is a polynomial of degree ≤ 2 in k². No denominator in k appears, so there is no tail.

Non-pole terms are four-χ contact interactions that field redefinitions can trade for explicit contact operators [T], so a gate placed in a (nonlocal) contact kernel G(s) would carry no X pole and no M_X dependence, and would not be X-exchange.

claims.statement: Read as an exact amplitude, #11 §8's form h(t)F(k²/μ²) with a t-channel pole in h has residue F(s), which is not a polynomial. The residue at a spin-J pole must be proportional to P_J(z_t) [T]. Both the Gaussian and the rational F have nonzero Legendre coefficients at every order computed, so the form would need exchanged particles of every spin at one mass. A single spin-2 X (or any finite-spin field) cannot produce it.

Beyond tree level, iterated exchange of a heavy X brings in k-scales of order M_X and Bohr-type scales, not μ. A scale μ appears only by tuning to a near-threshold state with 1/a = μ, which gives σ = 4πa²/(1 + k²a²): rational, saturating unitarity, and standard resonant SIDM (prior art †). At m = 70 MeV it gives σ/m = 9.8×10⁷ cm²/g, 3.3×10⁶ times the benchmark's 30 cm²/g. It is not the record's gate.
claims.basis: gate_numbers.py resonant block; standard effective-range expansion

claims.statement: Fiber overlap, reading R1 (the two quanta's one-body phase-space densities overlapping on the fiber with a kernel S of width μ). With momentum conservation, the fiber separation of the two bilinears equals a momentum transfer (k1 − k4 or k1 − k3). As an operator, ∫dx dp dp′ W(x,p) S(p−p′) W(x,p′) = 2π∫da db S̃(a−b) :n(a)n(b): + one-body terms: an ordinary x-local two-body potential of range ħ/μ = 9.87 pm. Its Born amplitude is S(q) + S(q_u). At q → 0 this is 1 + e^{−2k²/μ²}, so #6's e^{−(p1−p2)²/2μ²} is only the forward value of the exchange term, and the amplitude tends to 1, not 0, at large k. For wavepackets, the μ → 0 overlap is the state overlap, which falls with position separation exactly as it falls with momentum separation.

The vertex ∫dy g̃(y) χ(x+y/2) χ(x−y/2) sees the pair's relative momentum, and the separable amplitude is g(k)g*(k′) = |g(k)|² on shell: isotropic, and exactly §8's gate when the transfer factor is flat. claims.statement: The polarization is Lorentz-invariant. With Lorentzian g, ω, η, K, J, H and the Born rotation ρ = I are all invariant under L = diag(Λ, Λ^{−T}), while ρ flips K and J: the vacuum breaks ρ, not Lorentz symmetry. A Lorentz-invariant J therefore cannot make a t-channel vertex depend on anything but t, and it supplies no momentum scale. With the positive-definite H the compatibility theorem assumes, J and H are not Lorentz-invariant: positivity needs a preferred frame (OP3).

Because Σ|mV + k_i|² = 4m²V² + 4k², a per-leg profile then gives e^{−k²/μ²}·e^{−m²V²/μ²}: the record's gate multiplied by a suppression in the pair's velocity V through the frame. That suppression is 0.26, 4.7×10⁻⁶ and 4.9×10⁻²² at V = 100, 300 and 600 km/s. This gates on motion through the frame, not on relative velocity.

claims.statement: Q3. As a statement about a gate in k on the forward amplitude, #6 §4's 'tree-level exchange with generic vertices yields rational (power-law-tailed) gates' is false. The forward t-channel amplitude is a polynomial in k² that does not decrease (C2, C5). The rationality of tree amplitudes [T] sits in the transfer channel: the propagator 1/(q² + M_X²) and vertex form factors in t. Integrated over angle, these give a light mediator's σ_T(v) knee with a power-law tail, which is the 'standard expectation' of #11 §13 row 1, not a program-specific gate. At most, the sentence covers the u-channel exchange term of C6, which does not gate.

§8's 'the variable no x-local mediator produces' holds only for the direct Born term. Exchange terms (C6) and near-threshold states (C8) of x-local forces do depend on k at fixed q. §8 also assigns this variable to X, which §7 builds as an x-local field (δX_μν = ∂_(μ λ_ν); 'Yukawa-cut at 1/M_X', §7.5), so the sentence contradicts §7.

#13 §4 identifies μ ~ ħ/λ_χ, with λ_χ an irreducible extent in position. Standard form-factor physics then gives a form factor in the transfer q at scale μ [T], which is the x-space construction #6 calls the dual, not a gate in k.

Q4. The tag [D — mechanism; shape [O]] in #11 §8 is unsupported by the record. The fitting tag is [P] for the gate and μ (what #1 §3, v0.1, had), with the mechanism [O] and the negative result recorded: t-channel exchange of §7's X cannot produce the gate [D][V]. A conditional [D] is not available, because the only condition that yields the gate (a pair-channel kernel g(k)g(k′)) contains the gate and does not involve X. §14 item 4 ('Gate shape (X propagator on momentum fibers; Gaussian vs rational — now observable) [O]') does not cover what is missing: it treats the mechanism as settled, presupposes an object §7 does not have, and its Gaussian-vs-rational split is not a k-gate dichotomy (C10, C15). Text that depends on the tag includes the #11 abstract and §8 plain-language passage, §12 ('sharp tail'), §13 rows 1–3, §15 ('gate tail not yet forced'), HANDOFF §2 (alive list), #8 §5 ('mechanism found'), and the wiki's gate-mechanism page (status alive, [D]).

The record's benchmark arithmetic reproduces as contact Born physics, independent of any gate mechanism: σ₀ = 16πα̃²m²/m_φ⁴ with α̃ = 1 and m_φ = m_χ gives σ₀/m = 32.0 cm²/g at 70 MeV, or m = 71.5 MeV for 30 cm²/g. The convention values are μ/m = 2.857×10⁻⁴, v* = 121.1 km/s and v_a = √2 v* = 171.3 km/s.

open_questions: Does the program keep the gate as a postulate [P], or rewrite χ's self-interaction as an x-local potential of range ~10 pm (reading R1)? R1 is ordinary short-range SIDM with power-law tails and would remove the program-specific content of rows 1–3.
Can any construction tied to the program's geometry yield a pair-channel (s-channel) form factor for χχ, for example a doubly charged composite of the χ sector? Nothing in the record points to one.
If a Gaussian s-dependent form factor is kept, are microcausality and unitarity acceptable at the nonlocality scale ħ/μ ≈ 10 pm? Not examined here or in the record.

Would a doubled (phase-space) field theory for χ that drops the section condition, with fiber coordinates independent of the physical momentum, define a 'relative momentum' consistent with momentum conservation? The record does not address this.

Once the particle-side tail is not forced to be Gaussian, does the row-3 island discriminant survive? Under R1 the particle tail is a power law, the same functional class as the wave island's (v*/σ)⁴.
The strength of the coupling (OP5, the dual-stress enhancement) stays open whatever the mechanism; at gravitational strength, X-exchange is negligible in any case.

The main theorem is tree level on a flat background with the Fierz–Pauli numerator. Hassan–Rosen nonlinearities and vDVZ subtleties change the t-dependence and normalization, not the degree in s. Loops are treated through the effective-range argument and one number.

The section-condition and asymmetric-relic statements come from #1 (lab notebook), which is superseded as reference but is the only document that states them. #11 §12 and §14 item 7 keep polarization-genesis.
The Lorentzian check transplants the program's block structures to Lorentzian g; the record's theorems assume positive H (OP3).
Cross-section normalizations in fiber_overlap.py use unit couplings; only the shapes and tail laws are compared.

Gate convention used throughout: amplitude e^{−k²/μ²} = e^{−v²/v_a²} with v_a = √2 v* = 171.3 km/s; cross-section e^{−v²/v*²}. The √2 question of flag 17 is untouched by these conclusions.
